name: Regular insulin
executiveSummary: Regular (short-acting) insulin. Adult/ped DKA: bolus **0.05–0.1 units/kg** then **0.05–0.1 units/kg/h** IV. Neonatal hyperglycemia: **0.01–0.05 units/kg/h**. Hyperkalemia: **0.1 units/kg** with glucose.
indications:
## Indications

- Diabetic ketoacidosis and hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state.
- Glycemic control in ICU.
- Correction of hyperkalemia (with glucose).

## Practical identification

- Short-acting / regular (usual yellow label — confirm local packaging).
- Distinguish from NPH (intermediate).

## Precautions

- Hypoglycemia and hypokalemia. Frequent capillary glucose during infusion.

> Titrate per institutional DKA/ICU protocol.

adulto.dose: DKA: bolus **0.1 units/kg IV** then infusion **0.1 units/kg/h** titrated to glucose. Hyperkalemia: **10 units** IV with glucose (or **0.1 units/kg**).
adulto.administration: IV pump (dilute e.g. **1 unit/mL** in NS) or SC.
adulto.notes: Hold/reduce if glucose falls rapidly; replace K+ per DKA protocol.

pediatrico.dose: DKA: bolus **0.05–0.1 units/kg IV** then **0.05–0.1 units/kg/h**. Hyperkalemia: **0.1 units/kg** with glucose.
pediatrico.notes: Watch for hypoglycemia, tachycardia, pallor, hypokalemia.

neonatal.dose: Neonatal hyperglycemia: **0.01–0.05 units/kg/h** continuous IV; titrate to glucose.

stability:
## Stability

- Opened vial: ~28 days refrigerated (package insert). Diluted infusion: ~24 h.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Hypoglycemia, hypokalemia, rare allergy, lipodystrophy (chronic SC).
